$comment: Acme design tokens -- the source of truth for every design value.
Hand-edited. design/tokens/tokens.css is GENERATED from this file by
design/scripts/tokens/build_tokens.py -- edit here, then rerun it.
STUB: this is the template's neutral set (a grey scale and one accent).
Bootstrap replaces the values with the project's own and keeps the
structure and the comment pattern: each value says what it holds.
JSON has no comments, so a '$comment' key beside a value is the pattern.

colour.$comment: The grey scale, light to dark, and one accent. Names are steps, not roles: a role (page background, secondary text) is a 'semantic' entry below that points at a step. A step's contrast is measured on the page background (grey-50) and on white; text needs 4.5:1 or more (WCAG AA).

grey-100.use: Quiet surface: a hovered row, a table stripe

grey-200.use: Placeholder fill, a skeleton, a disabled control

grey-300.use: Strong border. Not for text: 1.4:1 on the page background

grey-500.use: Least-prominent text that still reads (placeholders, captions)

brand.use: The one accent: focus ring, links, a mark of the active item. Text or fill; white on it reads 6.7:1

semantic.$comment: Roles, not colours: a screen asks for 'muted', never for a grey step. A role may point at a colour step with var(--x), which keeps the two in step; a value with transparency is written out, because a step has none. line and soft are the text colour (grey-900) at 14% and 5%: a hairline border and a hover wash that stay visible on any surface.

state.$comment: Status colours for the few places a label is the right answer (a form error, a saved notice). fg on bg reads 5.4:1 or more for ok, info, warn and err; draft is the neutral one (6.2:1). Meaning never rests on colour alone: pair it with words or an icon.

ui.$comment: The one face, for headings and reading alike. 'Inter Variable' is the family name Fontsource declares; the package is bundled with the app (frontend/src/app/fonts.ts), so no font is fetched from a third party. It covers Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese; a project in a script it lacks (Hebrew, Arabic, CJK) swaps the package and this name at bootstrap. The rest of the stack is what shows while the font loads, and for any script the font lacks.

scale_px.$comment: Steps by sqrt(2), a ratio that doubles every two steps: 16 -> 22.6 -> 32 -> 45.3 -> 64. 100 is the reading size. The two steps below it: 075 = 16/2^(1/4) = 13.5, a half step, for captions, helper text and metadata; 050 = 16/sqrt(2) = 11.3, a full step, for short labels only -- counts, badges, timestamps, never running sentences. Form inputs stay at 16 or more (iOS Safari zooms the page on focus below 16). One-decimal rounding, like 22.6 and 45.3.

radius.$comment: Four radii and nothing in between. card is a surface (a card, a dialog), input a field, photo an image, pill a button or anything small that you tap.

motion.$comment: Fast (150ms), base (200ms) and slow (250ms): a state change should take between 150 and 250ms, quick enough not to be waited for and slow enough to be seen. Read by both the generated CSS (tokens.css) and frontend/src/lib/motion.ts's MOTION constant (the same numbers in seconds; pinned by theme-parity.test.ts). The ease curve cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) is Material's standard curve: it starts fast and settles.
